questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How our mood affects what we buy
Which country spends the most online
How to save money when shopping
Why people prefer shopping online
questions.why: Neil says they are looking at the link between shopping and mood.

options: He needed new clothes for work meetings
It was a close friend's birthday that week
There was a big sale on in the city centre
He felt miserable and wanted to cheer up
questions.why: Dan says he was feeling a bit miserable, so he went shopping to cheer himself up.

questions.q: What did the research by moneysupermarket.com find?
options: Happy people spend more money than sad or bored people
People shop much more at weekends than during the week
Sad, bored or stressed people often buy things they regret
Most people never regret what they buy, even when stressed
questions.why: It found people are more likely to buy things they'll regret when sad, bored or stressed.

questions.q: What does Sam buy when she feels down?
options: Wine and new shoes
Food, hot drinks and cosy things like a jumper
Books and magazines
Nothing, because she avoids shopping
questions.why: Sam says she buys food, warm drinks and warm, cosy things like a nice jumper.

questions.q: What does Phil say about bad days at work?
options: He goes straight to bed as soon as he gets home
He is more likely to buy something on the way home
He spends the whole evening shopping online for clothes
He calls a friend to talk about it instead of shopping
questions.why: Phil says after a bad day he is 'more likely to buy something on the way home'.

questions.q: What does Catherine notice about the clothes she buys when she's sad?
options: She never actually wears them
They are always too expensive
They are her favourite clothes
She usually takes them back to the shop
questions.why: She says the things she bought when she was sad, she never wears.

questions.q: Why does Neil find Catherine's comment interesting?
options: It shows she spends more than Dan
It proves retail therapy always works
It shows clothes are the most popular purchase
It matches exactly what the survey found
questions.why: Neil says 'that's exactly what the survey found': people regret purchases made when sad.

questions.q: What is Neil's attitude to retail therapy?
options: He does it all the time, just like Dan, and enjoys it
He only does it online, never in real shops in town
He avoids it because the good feeling doesn't last
He thinks it is the best cure for sadness and stress
questions.why: Neil says he tries to avoid it and doesn't think the happiness lasts very long.
